## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-*juan* Northern-Wèi (Yuán-Wèi) translation of [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) Vasubandhu's *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-upadeśa* by [勒那摩提](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8B%92%E9%82%A3%E6%91%A9%E6%8F%90) Ratnamati and [僧朗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%97) Sēnglǎng — the parallel translation to [菩提留支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E7%95%99%E6%94%AF) Bodhiruci's two-*juan* version at [KR6d0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0126) (T1519). The Taishō cross-reference 「No. 1520 [No. 1519]」 documents the parallel-translation pattern. Body attribution: *Pósǒupándòu púsà zào / Yuán-Wèi zhōng Tiānzhú sānzàng Lènàmótí gòng Sēnglǎng děng yì* 婆藪般豆菩薩造 / 元魏中天竺三藏勒那摩提共僧朗等譯.

**Abstract**

Ratnamati's translation of Vasubandhu's *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka-upadeśa* differs in significant respects from Bodhiruci's parallel translation ([KR6d0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0126), T1519): the Ratnamati version is more compressed (one *juan* vs. Bodhiruci's two), reflecting either a different Indic recension or different translation methodology. Modern critical study of the two translations remains valuable for the comparative reconstruction of the Indic original and for documenting the early sixth-century Sinitic Yogācāra translation tradition.

The doctrinal content is essentially the same: Vasubandhu's Yogācāra-school exposition of the Lotus Sūtra, providing the foundational Indic Mahāyāna commentary on which subsequent Sinitic Yogācāra readings of the Lotus ([窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) Kuījī's *Xuánzàn* [KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026) and the Cí'ēn subcommentarial tradition) were ultimately based.

The Ratnamati–Sēnglǎng translation is bracketed within Ratnamati's productive period at Luòyáng (c. 508–535).
